reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: 1 adds to one bucket in one subframe, coalesced: the bucket marked pending, flushed by a subframe-close callback
reading.floor: adaptive coalescing: a bucket's first change in a batch is written, settled and announced at once and the bucket is pushed once into a channel-owned array; later changes in the same subframe only flag it, and the outermost close writes and announces each flagged bucket once more, then runs its release check
reading.caveat: 1 adds to ONE bucket inside one subframe. No content-change listener. Every scenario here opens an outer subframe, so the adaptive arm always takes its batch path: the first change of each bucket costs what the immediate arm pays, and from the second change on it pays one flag write per add plus one more write and announce per bucket at the close. With a listener, the first announce is buffered by the owner's subframe and the second reaches the listener directly at the channel close, so a bucket changed more than once is heard twice. A single-item door with no outer subframe takes the immediate path and is not among these scenarios. One operation is one member add. Both arms open the same nested subframe around each add, push the member into the bucket store, and close the frame after every outer subframe; emptying the stores there is timed on both arms alike. The bucket slot is held and has one effect, so the channel write door takes its effect path: the first write of a frame schedules the effect and the rest find it scheduled. The bodies copy OIMBucketWriter.markBucketSlotChanged, OIMChannel.writeWithoutFlushCheck and closeSubframe, and OIMSlotContentOwner.settleWrite, contentChanged and its subframe delivery, as of 2026-10-21. The release policy is the default one, which does nothing on a write, so neither arm calls it.
